images.title: Seedlings in rows of 13
images.purpose: Show the method cue for lowest terms: find the biggest number that fits into both top and bottom, here 13 in 26/39, so the student can repeat it on the big fractions.
images.composition: One wide seedling tray in the upper half with generous margins, and one short factor row centred below it.
images.exact_structure: Top: one flat rectangular seedling tray of exactly 39 equal square cells in 3 rows of 13. The top 2 rows, 26 cells, each hold a small sprout filled teal #0072B2; the bottom row of 13 cells is plain and empty. A thin reddish purple #CC79A7 bracket at the right end marks each of the 3 rows as one group of 13. Below, centred: one factor row of two short lines, 26 = 2 × 13 above 39 = 3 × 13, with the 13s in reddish purple. Exactly 1 tray, 39 cells, 26 sprouts, 1 factor row.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any of the four big fractions or their simplified forms shown anywhere
images.takeaway: Divide top and bottom by the biggest number that fits into both.
images.description: A seedling tray of 3 rows of 13 cells with 2 rows sprouted shows 26/39; the factor row 26 = 2 × 13 and 39 = 3 × 13 shows why 26/39 = 2/3 in lowest terms.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at one row of 13 and say how many rows are sprouted out of how many, before trying the big fractions.

image_decisions.why: Rows of 13 make the shared factor visible; one picture gives the method without solving any part of the question.
